title: Runtime compatibility and lifecycle policy (semver, LTS, rollouts)
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: Establish a clear, executable semantic versioning and lifecycle policy for the Redwood inference runtime so teams can plan upgrades, communicate breaking changes, and automate safe rollouts. Scope covers runtime binary/API surface (gRPC/HTTP), persisted on-disk formats (KV cache checkpoints, model artifacts), admin config semantics, plugin/extension compat, and upgrade tooling.

Summary of rules: 
- Semantic versioning model is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. MAJOR bumps indicate incompatible or breaking changes to runtime public behavior (protocols, on-disk format, public API contract). MINOR bumps introduce backward-compatible features and deprecations. PATCH bumps are for bug fixes and non-behavioral changes.
- Deprecation: any API/behavior slated for removal must be announced and emit runtime deprecation warnings for at least two consecutive MINOR releases before removal in a MAJOR release. Deprecation announcement must include migration plan and migration tooling.
- LTS channels: we will maintain a single LTS channel per MAJOR (e.g., 2.x-lts). LTS windows are 12 months from LTS cut or until the next LTS is cut, whichever is longer. Only PATCH-level and critical-security MINOR backports are allowed on LTS. LTS releases will be clearly documented and have dedicated release notes and upgrade guides.
- Rollout gates: every release must define automated rollout gates (canary -> ramp -> full). Critical metrics (p50/p95 latency, error rate, OOMs, token throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, tail-latency spikes) and thresholds must be declared in the release PR. A single SLO regression of more than the configured threshold triggers automatic rollback.
- Upgrade tooling: provide a first-class CLI and CI preflight for upgrades (rdi-upgrade) with dry-run and fast-rollback capabilities. Preflight checks include config compatibility, model artifact checksum validation, KV checkpoint compatibility, and smoke requests against canary endpoints.

Intended usage: This policy is the baseline for release engineers, platform/product teams, and customers operating Private/Dedicated deployments. It is prescriptive for hosted releases and recommended for private deployments (we provide the same tooling).
acceptance_criteria: Policy text codified in repo under docs/release/semver-lifecycle.md
CI enforces: every release PR includes a semver rationale (breaking vs non-breaking) and declared rollout gates
rdi-upgrade CLI includes --dry-run, --preflight, and --rollback subcommands and is validated in a test harness
LTS policy documented with support window and backport rules and published to operators and account teams
Automated rollback rules implemented in the release controller: threshold-based rollback on latency (+10% p95) or error-rate (+0.5% absolute) regressions by default

Add CI checker to require semver rationale label on release PRs
Instrument release controller to read rollout gate config from release manifest
Implement rdi-upgrade preflight checks and dry-run mode (unit + integration tests)
Publish LTS support calendar and create template for LTS cut procedure

rollout_gates: Canary: 1% traffic for 30 minutes with full telemetry; must pass preflight smoke tests
Ramp: 10% for 1 hour, 25% for 2 hours, 50% for 6 hours - stop condition if any gate fails
Full: remaining traffic only after Ramp gates pass for at least 24 hours
Automatic rollback triggers: p95 latency increase > 10% (absolute) OR error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points OR OOM/crash rate > 0.1%
Manual hold: product or SRE can pause rollout; release owner must provide action plan within 2 hours
upgrade_tooling: Preflight checks: config schema validation, model artifact checksum, KV checkpoint compatibility test, sample request/response smoke test
Migration helper libs for safe on-the-fly transformations of KV checkpoints with reversible mode
Blue/green and canary deployment helpers integrated with release controller; audit logging of each step
SDK compatibility matrix generator: produce per-SDK compatibility table for each runtime MINOR release
